paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God keeps calling His people back, even when they've run off a long way. Israel chased other gods, Judah watched it happen and did the same, and God still says, "Return, O faithless Israel" (Jeremiah 3:12). He says, "I will no longer look on you with anger, for I am merciful" (Jeremiah 3:12). And what does He ask for? "Only acknowledge your guilt" (Jeremiah 3:13).

Now look at how much God wants this. He says, "How I long to make you My sons," and He thought they would call Him "Father" (Jeremiah 3:19). Then He says, "Return, O faithless children, and I will heal your faithlessness" (Jeremiah 3:22). Friend, He doesn't just wave the wrongdoing away. He heals it, and the people answer, "Here we are. We come to You, for You are the LORD our God" (Jeremiah 3:22).

But the return has to be real. Judah came back "only in pretense" (Jeremiah 3:10), and God asks for hearts that are really turned: "Circumcise yourselves to the LORD, and remove the foreskins of your hearts" (Jeremiah 4:4). The warning is serious, because wrath that burns with no one to put it out is heavy. So here's my question for you, baker: is there something you've been drifting from? The door is open, and the word God keeps calling out is return.
